events.title: Laban kisses his family and returns home
events.narrative_summary: Early in the morning Laban kisses his sons and daughters, blesses them and goes back to his place.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Laban rose early in the morning' (32:1): the morning after the covenant night (evt.gen_31.covenant_feast, which stayed the night). Anchored on its END with BOKER; the farewell takes about an hour.

events.title: Angels of God meet Jacob and he names Mahanaim
events.narrative_summary: Jacob goes on his way and angels of God meet him. Seeing them he says 'This is God's camp' and calls the place Mahanaim.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Jacob leaves the Gilead hill country after Laban and reaches Mahanaim, a day or so of travel with flocks and children (Onkelos and Pseudo-Jonathan add nothing on timing); offset 1 day, margin 1 day, from Laban's departure END.

events.title: Jacob sends messengers to Esau in Edom
events.narrative_summary: Jacob sends messengers ahead to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom, with words of submission and a report of his wealth, seeking favour.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the naming of Mahanaim directly; no delay stated. Starts at the END of the angels event, margin 1 day; the instructions take about an hour.

events.title: Messengers report Esau is coming with 400 men
events.narrative_summary: The messengers return to Jacob and say that Esau is coming to meet him with four hundred men.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No duration in the text. urim travel Mahanaim to Edom, 'hurry': about 200 km by road, 40 h moving, ~4 days each way. Esau is already marching toward Jacob (32:7), so the round trip is shorter than 8 days: offset 6 days, margin 3 days.

events.title: Jacob, afraid, divides his people into two camps
events.narrative_summary: Jacob is greatly afraid and distressed. He divides his people, flocks, herds and camels into two camps, reasoning that if Esau strikes one the other may escape.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediate reaction to the report (32:8), so it starts at the END of the report with no delay; dividing a household and herds takes about 3 hours.

events.title: Jacob prays to be delivered from Esau
events.narrative_summary: Jacob prays to the God of Abraham and Isaac, confesses he is unworthy of God's kindness, asks to be saved from Esau, and recalls God's promise of good and countless descendants.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The prayer follows the division of the camps (his words 'I have become two camps', 32:11); no delay is stated, so it starts at the END of the division. A short prayer, about 20 minutes.

events.title: Jacob lodges and selects a gift for Esau
events.narrative_summary: Jacob lodges there that night and takes from what he has a gift for Esau: goats, sheep, camels, cattle and donkeys.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'He lodged there that night' (32:14): evening after the prayer, so EREV from the END of the prayer (the prayer ends mid-afternoon in the chain, so the evening is the same day); the selection takes about 2 hours.

events.title: Jacob sends the gift in droves with instructions
events.narrative_summary: Jacob gives each drove to a servant, tells them to go ahead with a space between droves, and tells each what to say if Esau asks whose they are: a gift from Jacob, who is behind them.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous with the choosing of the gift on the same evening; starts at its END, about 2 hours to divide the droves and give the instructions.

events.title: The gift crosses ahead while Jacob stays in the camp
events.narrative_summary: The gift goes on ahead of Jacob, and he spends that night in the camp.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The execution of the preceding instructions the same evening (32:22 'that night'); starts at their END, about half an hour to set off.

events.title: Jacob rises by night and sends his family over the Jabbok
events.narrative_summary: That night Jacob gets up, takes his two wives, two maids and eleven sons across the ford of the Jabbok, and sends over all he has.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'He rose in that night' (32:23). Radak: after a little sleep. Offset 90 minutes after the gift left puts the start near midnight; margin 2 hours; crossing a household and herds about 2 hours (stay in camp is in 32:22).

events.title: A man wrestles with Jacob until dawn and wrenches his hip
events.narrative_summary: Jacob is left alone and a man wrestles with him until dawn. Seeing he cannot prevail, the man touches the socket of Jacob's thigh and it is put out of joint.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Until the coming up of the dawn' (32:25; Ibn Ezra: the end of night's darkness, or the glow before sunrise). Starts when the crossing ends (about 02:00) and runs 3 hours; the dawn scene follows at SHACHAR. Pseudo-Jonathan's expansion (the angel speaking of tithes) is not used.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: Until the breaking of the day

events.title: Jacob demands a blessing and is renamed Israel
events.narrative_summary: The man asks to be let go because the dawn has come, but Jacob will not release him until he blesses him. He asks Jacob's name, renames him Israel for striving with God and men and prevailing, refuses to give his own name, and blesses him there.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Let me go, for the dawn has come up' (32:27) fixes it at first light: SHACHAR after the wrestling, DIURNAL_HOUR. The exchange takes about 20 minutes.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: For the dawn has come up

events.title: Jacob names the place Peniel
events.narrative_summary: Jacob calls the place Peniel, saying he has seen God face to face and his life is preserved.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediately after the blessing (32:31), no delay; a moment's action of 5 minutes, same dawn scene.

events.title: The sun rises on Jacob limping past Penuel
events.narrative_summary: As Jacob passes Penuel the sun rises on him and he limps because of his thigh.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'The sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel' (32:32): sunrise, BOKER, snapped after the naming; lasts about an hour while he moves on.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Having been blessed and having seen God face to face, Jacob names the place Peniel (32:31).
Hearing that Esau comes with 400 men, Jacob is afraid and divides his camp (32:8).
Fear of Esau's approach leads Jacob to prepare a gift to appease him (32:14, 32:21).
Jacob's messengers go to Esau and come back with his answer (32:7).
Jacob's commands to the servants are carried out as the gift goes on ahead (32:22).
Because Jacob held on and would not let the man go without a blessing, he receives the name Israel (32:27-29).
The dislocated thigh socket makes Jacob limp as the sun rises (32:26, 32:32).
